note: The main banks, chosen as the best-known large card issuers (no central bank ranking was read): National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr and CIB. National Bank of Egypt's card pages answered behind a Cloudflare check and CIB's behind an Incapsula check on 2026-10-30, and neither was read. Banque Misr's credit card fees, usage limits, commissions and interest rates (dated 1 September 2026), read in full on 2026-10-30 (first read 2026-10-29 for the Classic alone): each personal credit card's issuance fee for the first year and its renewal fee, equal for every card but El Araby's and written as a yearly fee (Classic, Islamic Classic, Gold and Islamic Gold 250 pounds, Titanium 350, Platinum 500, Signature and World 2,500, World Elite and Visa Infinite 8,000, Visa Infinite Private free; El Araby 100 to issue and 50 to renew, written as a yearly fee of 50 waived for the first year and an issue fee of 100). The conventional cards bear 4% a month on a decreasing balance; the Islamic cards and El Araby 20.55% a year, fixed. A cash withdrawal at Banque Misr's ATMs costs 2% with a minimum of 15 pounds on the conventional cards and 5% with a minimum of 50 on the Islamic ones (other banks' and foreign ATMs cost more and aren't written); the 'outside fees' on cash and purchases abroad are 3%; the late payment and overdrawn fees are 75 pounds each. The Business card isn't written (not a personal card), nor the Islamic Titanium, whose fee column the table doesn't print separately, nor the Asatha card, whose interest rate the table doesn't give, nor the instalment card. The schedule states no minimum payment or grace period; interest on purchases runs from the purchase date only on the unpaid amount. Wave 4 (2026-10-30): HSBC Bank Egypt was added, a large card issuer whose schedule of services and tariffs answers this research (QNB Egypt answered with a Cloudflare check, Arab African International Bank with 'Request Rejected', ADIB Egypt and Alexbank showed checks or forms and weren't read; National Bank of Egypt and CIB weren't retried). Its schedule of services and tariffs (the web page, read in full on 2026-10-30): the Visa Evolution, Visa Platinum and Cashback cards are free when a year's purchases reach 20,000, 45,000 or 30,000 pounds and otherwise cost 300, 450 or 400 a year (written as a yearly fee waived on that spending); the Advance and Premier Mastercards, for the bank's Advance and Premier customers (a condition the game doesn't check), are free. The monthly finance charge is 4.42% (4.00% on the Premier Mastercard); a cash advance costs 5%, at least 75 pounds; the FX mark-up is 3%; the late payment fee is 150. The monthly maintenance fee for cardholders without an HSBC account (16 pounds, deducted quarterly) isn't written: the game doesn't check where the holder banks. The schedule states no minimum payment or grace period. Banque du Caire was added too, a large state-owned bank whose tariff answers this research. Its schedule of charges for individuals (19-10-2026), the credit cards, read in full: each main card's issuance fee and its equal annual fee, written as a yearly fee as Banque Misr's are (Classic, Visa or MasterCard, 250 pounds; Gold 300; Titanium 400; Platinum 650; World Elite 8,000; the Visa and MasterCard of a tier share one row and are written as one card); a monthly interest rate of 4.30% on every card; a cash withdrawal fee of 4%, at least 50 pounds, at its own and other banks' ATMs in Egypt (6% plus 60 abroad, not written); a mark-up of 3%; and a late payment fee of 7% of the minimum payment, at least 100 and at most 200. Its over-limit fee of 2% (at least 100) doesn't say what the 2% is of and isn't written; nor is the 10-pound monthly SMS fee, which the tariff doesn't make mandatory. It states no minimum payment or grace period.
